title: Wanted by Angelica Chéri and Ross Baum on Broadway #wantedmusical #wa...
transcript: As Black women with no real socioeconomic mobility afforded to them in 1893, Mary and Martha Clark take matters into their own hands, using their light skin to pass as upper class white women. It seems like such an outlandish plot for a Broadway musical, but it's also a true story. I didn't see this show in its first iteration as Gun and Powder at Paper Mill, and this was only the second Broadway preview, so I can't speak to what's still actively being worked on. What I can say is it's clear that time, love, and care has been put into the writing and the structure of this musical. It's most evident in the efficient and witty book and the brassy score that fits these performers like a glove. It is dense and melodically satisfying, and brings out the vocal pyrotechnics without muddying the storytelling. Another highlight for me was Solea Pfeiffer, who is absolutely radiant in her vocal performance and her depiction of Mary's internal struggle throughout the piece. When she gets a taste of the possibilities she'd have as a wealthy white woman, she romanticizes it and sings a joyous tune called “Real Woman.” It's a stunning moment in the first act, but layered on top of the sad and uncomfortable truth it exposes. Along these lines, even though the story is set in 1893, the way it centers biracial women opens up a really interesting conversation about assimilation that is still relevant today. While Act 1 of this show is really tight, Act 2 definitely has some room for improvement. Between a handful of clunky moments and the fact that the best songs appear in Act 1, the second act does drag a bit — but hey, that's what previews are for.
classificationReason: Creator clearly attended the second Broadway preview of 'Wanted' (originally Gun and Powder at Paper Mill) and shares first-hand opinions on the book, score, and Solea Pfeiffer's performance. Matches 'wanted-2022' on the list.
